dept.name: Department of Architecture
dept.tagline: All 15 semesters of the 207-credit B.Arch as BRACU prints them - the ten design studios, the technical spine, the five electives, the internship and the thesis - with a studio-first toolkit and a tracker that counts on BRACU's scale.
dept.contact: See the Department of Architecture page on bracu.ac.bd for the current contact
skills: Year 1
Drawing by hand every day: the graphics stream (ARC 111, ARC 112) and Design I-II (ARC 101, ARC 102) are won with a sketchbook that is never empty.
A model-making habit: card, foam and glue before any software, photographed well.
History as a timeline you can draw (ARC 122, ARC 123) and the words to talk about a building (ARC 121).
The studio rhythm: pin-up, reviews and critique, final presentation, portfolio - learned in semester one, repeated fifteen times.
Year 2
CAD and computer graphics (ARC 113, ARC 214) and digital visualisation (ARC 315) used for your own studio, not just the exercises.
Climate, light and sound as design inputs (ARC 251, ARC 252) that show up in the Design III-V schemes.
Structure I-II and Construction I-II (CEE 211, CEE 212, ARC 241, ARC 242) carried into the studio: a detail you can draw at 1:20.
A portfolio PDF built the department's way after every studio - 20 pages, under 10 MB, uploaded on time.
Year 3
Working drawings (ARC 311, ARC 312) and services (CEE 213, EEE 345, MEE 344) - the part of the office that pays the bills.
Urbanism and urban design (ARC 232, ARC 331) and the environment (ARC 412, ARC 452) feeding Design VI.
Bengal's own architecture (ARC 327, ARC 431) read on site, not only in slides.
Two electives chosen, and a firm shortlisted for ARC 300.
Year 4-5
ARC 300 Practical Training: a trainee log book kept daily and the oral assessment prepared.
Design VII-VIII (ARC 401, ARC 402) with estimation, specifications and structure (ARC 413, ARC 441, CEE 411) in the drawings, not beside them.
ARC 511 chapter submissions and the ARC 512 pre-thesis dissertation leading into ARC 502/503 Design X.
Professional practice and construction management (ARC 541, MGT 511) understood - and the two years of experience after graduation that the IAB asks for, planned.
dept.career_intro: The programme page says the B.Arch is accredited by the University Grants Commission and the Institute of Architects, Bangladesh, that graduates become eligible for full IAB membership after two years' work experience, and that the five-year coursework earns advanced standing in some master's degrees. The directions below are the common ones; none is a BRACU rule.
careers: Architectural practice
Design and documentation in a firm, towards IAB membership and your own practice.
Design I-X, the working-drawings stream (ARC 311, 312), ARC 541 Professional Practice; the ARC 300 internship log; a portfolio a stranger can read in five minutes.
Urban design and planning
Neighbourhoods, public space, city-scale projects with authorities and NGOs.
ARC 232 Urbanism, ARC 331 Urban Design, ARC 401 Design VII (the urban design studio), ARC 432 Housing and Development, ARC 492 The City in Development.
Interior and landscape design
Interiors, retail, hospitality, gardens and public landscapes.
ARC 411 Interior Design, ARC 412 Landscape Design, ARC 252 Lighting and Acoustical Design; a photographed built or furnished project.
Conservation and heritage
Documenting, restoring and reusing historic buildings.
ARC 327 History of Bengal Art and Architecture, ARC 491 Architectural Conservation, the five history courses, measured drawings from a study tour.
Sustainable and climate-responsive design
Buildings that work in Bangladesh's climate and for its risks.
ARC 251 Design with Climate, ARC 452 Design with the Environment, ARC 392 Tropical Architecture, ARC 393 Building for Disasters, ARC 494 Ecology and Sustainable Development.
Construction, project and cost management
The side of the industry that builds what is drawn.
ARC 413 Estimation, ARC 441 Specifications, MGT 511 Construction Management, ACT 511 Accounting, Structure I-VI.
Visualisation, fabrication and digital design
Rendering, animation, digital fabrication, BIM.
ARC 315 Digital Visualization, ARC 214, ARC 495 Computers in Architecture, the Fab Lab's laser cutter, 3D printer, 3D scanner and 5-axis CNC router.
Research, teaching and higher study
A master's with advanced standing, research, teaching studio.
ARC 522 Research Methods, ARC 511-512, a Thesis-stream Design X (ARC 502), ARC 493 Contemporary Architectural Thought, two recommenders who have reviewed your work.
career_notes: The Tuition and Fees page bills 'ARC (Studio Course Fee)' at Tk 8,800 a credit and 'ARC (Lecture Course Fee)' at Tk 8,250, but does not list which courses are studio; the Degree Planner treats Design I-X and the elective studios ARC 291-294 as studio courses, from the course descriptions and the 'Elective Studio Courses' heading, so confirm your bill with the Registrar. The page prints 207 credits; its semester rows and five electives add to 205, and a line 'ARC 231 Concepts in Planning' is printed in Semester 06 without a credit figure. Part 1 keeps BRACU's 207 and flags the gap - ask your advisor what fills it.

The department's Detail page describes internships that have expanded from India to Europe, the Americas and Southeast Asia, a Fabrication Lab, electives in painting, sculpture, photography and music appreciation, study tours to North Bengal and India, the Noman Award of Excellence in Design, the Rafiq Azam Travel Bursary, the Moitree cultural forum, the Angan lecture series and Town Hall meetings twice a semester. The Residential Semester at Savar has Architecture students designing installations in the open fields. None of these is printed with a rule or a date - ask the department office each semester.

rules.retake_note: BRACU's published rules (read Oct 2026): after an F a course may be retaken twice (a third time by exception of the Head or Dean) and the policy page says the best grade counts; a passed course may be repeated once within two semesters of first enrolment and the latest grade counts. The separate retake-and-repeat page caps a retaken or repeated course at B+ and limits repeats to grades of B- or below. A retake or repeat in the previous or current semester also makes you ineligible for the merit waiver. Weigh that before you repeat a passing grade.

Every semester row is printed with credits, but the rows sum to 195 and the five 2-credit electives add 10, giving 205 against the printed total of 207; the page prints no per-semester or per-category totals, no prerequisites and no semester for the electives, so copy the missing 2 credits and your elective semesters from your advising sheet.
facts: "The total credit requirement for the degree of Bachelor of Architecture is 207 credits"; "A regular student should take about 15 credits per semester" and, depending on academic standing and the advisor's recommendation, "a student may take a maximum of 21 credits per semester"; "the length of study for the degree is recommended to be 5 years (15 semesters)".

Studio courses: the design studios Design I-X (ARC 101 4.5, ARC 102 4.5, ARC 201 6, ARC 202 6, ARC 301 8, ARC 302 8, ARC 401 10, ARC 402 10, ARC 501 12, ARC 502/503 12 = 81 credits) and the elective studios ARC 291-ARC 294 are billed at the Tuition and Fees page's "ARC (Studio Course Fee) 8,800" per credit, against "ARC (Lecture Course Fee) 8,250" for lecture courses; the fee page itself does not list which courses count as studio, so confirm your bill with the Registrar.

MAT 091 and ENG 091 (0 credit) "Has to be taken, only if assigned in University Admission Test Viva"; "Only one of the courses (ENG 101 or ENG 102) is to be taken as assigned in University Admission Viva"; "Students who completed ENG 091, can only take ENG 101".

"Students need to complete a total of 5 elective courses from the list below" (2 credits each) and "They are suggested to take two (2) elective studio courses and three (3) elective lecture courses"; no elective is placed in any semester.
ARC 300 Practical Training (3 credits, Semester 11) is an "Internship at various local and international architectural firms", assessed by "Trainee Log Book and Oral communication".

ARC 512 Seminar II (Semester 14) is the pre-thesis course: "This course is to facilitate students in selecting their final thesis or project of Design X, arc 502/503" (project proposal, case studies, literature review, programme formulation, initial design development, written up as a dissertation); ARC 511 Seminar I (Semester 13) is assessed by assignments and chapter submissions.

ARC 501 Design IX runs in two streams (technical bias / socio-cultural bias); ARC 502/503 Design X "is the final studio, leading towards the Bachelor of Architecture degree" with a Thesis stream (ARC 502, analytical and research-based) and a Design Project stream (ARC 503, a practical site).

Juries: studios are assessed by "Reviews/critique" and "Final Presentation", the Muzharul Islam Gallery "provides students with open spaces for jury sessions", and every studio ends with a portfolio (maximum 20 pages, one PDF not exceeding 10 Mb) uploaded to the BRAC University Institutional Repository; students of ARC 302, ARC 401, ARC 402, ARC 501 and ARC 502 also submit additional drawings (all files within 30 MB).

The programme is accredited by the University Grants Commission of Bangladesh (UGC) and the Institute of Architects, Bangladesh (IAB); graduates become eligible for full IAB membership after 2 years' work experience.

Admission test for Architecture: "English (Composition and MCQ), Mathematics MCQ and Drawing"; minimum GPA 3.5 in SSC/equivalent and HSC/equivalent; candidates must pass each sub-section separately and are called for an interview for final selection.

Fees on the Tuition and Fees page ("for new students enrolled from Spring -2027"): admission fee 33,900 (one time), library membership fee 2,500 (one time), semester fee "ARC 14,175"; the freshman table prices one ARC lecture course at Tk. 24,750.

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole Architecture degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Architecture as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.
Open the **Toolkit** when the work starts: labs, projects, cases, the final-year runway.

book.text: Your data

Everything you type stays in this browser on this device - nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account and no internet is needed. That also means a cleared browser or a new phone starts empty. So, now and then, open **More** and tap **Save this planner with my data inside**: you get this same file back with everything you have typed written into it. Keep that copy - open it on a laptop, send it to a new phone, or hand it to next semester's you.

If a browser refuses to keep your data between visits (some phones open files in a way that forgets), Home tells you so and offers the same button. Your planner is then simply the latest copy you saved.

items: I have saved a copy with my data inside once, so I know where the button is.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: the Toolkit tab - The Architecture toolkit

Architecture at BRACU is ten studios in a row, assessed by reviews, critique and a final presentation, closed by a portfolio - with a technical spine, an internship and a thesis around them. Eight tools, studio first.
1. The studio spine, the load and the five electives

Ten design studios carry **81 of the 207 credits**: Design I to Design X, from 4.5 credits in Semester 01 to 12 in Semesters 13 and 15. The page says a regular student takes about **15 credits a semester**, at most **21** with good standing and the advisor's recommendation, over **15 semesters in five years**. The studio is the course that decides the semester - plan everything else around it.

ARC 501 Design IX runs in two streams - technical bias (structural or building-system complexity) and socio-cultural bias; ARC 502/503 Design X is the final studio, Thesis (ARC 502) or Design Project (ARC 503), chosen through ARC 512 Seminar II (tool 8).
Five electives of 2 credits

The page says 'Students need to complete a total of 5 elective courses' and suggests two elective studio courses and three elective lecture courses; it places none of them in a semester. The light semesters by the printed rows are 07 (11 credits), 09 (9.5), 11 (ARC 300 only, 3) and 14 (7.5) - the natural homes.

The printed semester rows add to 195 credits and the electives to 10 - 205 against the page's 207. the Degree tab keeps 207 and flags the two missing credits; ask your advisor whether 'ARC 231 Concepts in Planning', printed in Semester 06 without a credit, is the answer.

The page lists studio assessment as **'Reviews/critique'** and **'Final Presentation'**, with the Muzharul Islam Gallery as the open space for jury sessions, dedicated studio space for every design studio, a Computer Lab with 'virtually unlimited printing', and a Fab Lab with a laser cutter, 3D printer, 3D scanner and 5-axis CNC router. A studio is lost in week three, not in the final week: fill this on the day you receive the brief.
